items.title: 61427_Happy Caldwell oral history interview
items.q: So they put her -- Ella with us... So we saw the potentials in Ella.

ctx.x: Oh. Well, how long did you go with that?

We stayed there two years, until they got too big for himself and wanted to try to buck the booking agent -- that was wrong. See, what happened, when Ella Fitzgerald, after she won the amateur contest at the Apollo, we were going -- we had left Chicago, came on through Chicago, through Ohio, through Pennsylvania, back to New York. And we went into the Harlem -- the Opera House, which is boarded up now, on 126th Street and 7th Avenue. And that's when -- those were the amateur contests. They were giving them every…

So they put her -- Ella with us. She won it there (with Chick Webb) so they put her with Tiny Bradshaw's band. She was unknown then. And she was singing a song, and I was back in the section, and the thing was a big hit because her (unintelligible) back from the whatchacallit place in Chicago all the time. That's where she got the knack of wanting to sing. So we saw the potentials in Ella. So they -- when she came up, I said, (unintelligible), I said, you going to make it. Said, why?
